name: plate-49-engine-reprint-2c
version_tag: PATCHED 2026-08-08 — AS COMMITTED THIS PLATE WOULD HAVE PRINTED ENTIRELY BLACK. Four parts carried extruder=2 (150_board_daynums_white, 154/155/156_sat_ink) but NO filament_2 was declared, so _add_second_filament never runs, every per-extruder list stays length 1, and the slicer silently prints the whole plate in slot 1 — black day numbers on a black board and three black satellite inks, invisible. It would have PASSED the audit too: the existing gate only catches plates that DECLARE two filaments and then load one. Fixed by declaring filament_2 = white PLA Basic. NOTE THE SUB-BRAND: white on this printer is BASIC, not Matte, so ams_sub_brand_2 resolution must not be copied from the black filament. AMS ASSIGNMENT (Ron: 'white for the lettering, black for everything else'): T0 = black PLA Matte -> TRAY 3, T1 = white PLA Basic -> TRAY 0, i.e. ams_mapping [3, 0]. THE BRIEF SAID 'slot 1 black / slot 2 white' AND THAT IS REVERSED FROM THE MACHINE — live trays are slot1 white Basic, slot2 grey Matte, slot3 EMPTY, slot4 black Matte. This is the third time a stated layout has been backwards (plate-45 and plate-47 both did it); map by live tray_color, never by the sentence. flush_volume 364 = 1.3x the 280 used on plate-45. | #152 + #153 ENGINE REPRINT, TWO COLOUR — board + day numbers and all three labelled receivers + their ink. SUPERSEDES everything from plate-43/45/47: those parts were correct when printed but the spec moved under them twice. #147 raised the band pitch 5.0 -> 6.5, which makes the board's month post taller; #148 replaced the single shared strike-bar bearing (E1_BASE 6.0, unchanged since #110) with a per-satellite one, because the three satellites strike on different dates (month 30, feb 29, leap 28) and cannot share a phase — feb was 306% and leap 213% of the 1.12mm drive window out of position, so February would never have been shortened and the leap tooth would never have fired. #152 STEPPED POST: the board's month post now runs full 5.40 through the satellite that rides it, then a 0.60mm SHOULDER, then a 4.20 spigot the carrier arm bottoms against. That shoulder is the point — the arm used to seat on the ROTATING satellite's top face across a 0.20 running clearance, so it had no datum at all, which is the float Ron felt at the bench. Grip goes 0.52 -> 0.67 diameters and the #146 pad overhang shrinks 1.29 -> 0.79. #153 TEXT: satellite stroke 0.45 -> 0.42 (exactly one outer-wall bead at a 0.4 nozzle — between 1 and 2 beads the slicer alternates between one fat bead and two starved ones along a curve, which is most of what makes a stroke font look ragged), and the engraving depth 0.50 -> 0.40, two WHOLE layers at 0.20 instead of two and a half, which had been rounding unpredictably and varying the letter depth across the wheel. Depth went DOWN not up on strength: the groove sits in a 1.5mm bar that takes the drive impulse. Legibility does not suffer because the contrast comes from the white filament, not the depth. Board text left ALONE at stroke 0.70 — it is proven on hardware and not worth regressing for a marginal gain. Seam set ALIGNED (on a letter counter the loop is a few mm round, so a scattered seam blob is a large fraction of it), precise_outer_wall on, outer wall 40 and top surface 30, flush multiplier 1.3 to stop black bleeding into the white inlay. NO IRONING — it smears one filament across the other on a two-colour top surface. AMS slot 1 BLACK, slot 2 WHITE. Each ink body carries its OWN registration offset from its host because compose centres every object on its own bbox and those centres differ — do not tidy them. 8 objects, flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06. | QUIET.
